warnings: Original registry outcome, arm denominator, adverse event and p-value fields are source-reported data, not independent analysis.
No source model effect size, statistical significance, clinical benefit, safety conclusion or FDA outcome is computed or certified.
Source SHA256 fingerprints identify exact raw public API response bytes at this retrieval time; they do not verify final signed SAPs or the clinical study report.
Primary outcome counts shown are ORIGINAL CURRENT POSTED results; pre-specification requires prospectively signed original SAP/amendment and blinded first-access timeline.
Serious AE term counts and source affected/at-risk groups are not independent denominator or exposure-window reconciliation.
The 17 other FOCUS trials have R89/R90 journal, issuer or SEC report leads but no posted aggregate results in prior current-registry snapshot; do not call these failed or omitted studies.

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Proportion of Subjects Who Achieve Clinical Remission Per Modified Mayo Score at Week 8
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: To compare the efficacy of ABX464 versus placebo on clinical remission. Clinical remission is defined as stool frequency subscore (SFS) = 0 or 1 and rectal bleeding subscore (RBS) = 0, and Mayo Endoscopic Score (MES) = 0 or 1 (MES of 1 modified to exclude friability).

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Change From Baseline in Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI)
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: AHI, Apnea-Hypopnea Index, is the number of apneas or hypopneas recorded via polysomnography during the study per hour of sleep. Apnea is defined as a cessation of airflow lasting at least 10 seconds, hypopnea as a decrease in airflow by at least 30% from baseline for at least 10 seconds occurring with a drop in oxygen saturation (SpO2) by at least 4%.
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.populationDescription: The Full Analysis Set (FAS) population included all randomized participants who received at least one dose of investigational medicinal product (IMP). Participants enrolled at Site 1308 were excluded following site termination. The While-On-treatment population was the MITT set and includes participants in the FAS who had at least one post-baseline on-treatment polysomnography (PSG) assessment.

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Number of Patients With Loss of Response With Respect to Hypertension During the RW Phase.
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Week 22 (end of OL Phase) and Week 36 (Week 12 of RW Phase)
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: Loss of response with respect to HTN was measured using 6 criteria: 1) an increase in SBP of at least 5 mm Hg, 2) an increase in DBP of at least 5 mm Hg, 3) an increase in SBP and/or DBP of at least 5 mm Hg, 4) use of HTN rescue medication, 5) treatment discontinuation, and 6) missing 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) measurement at the end of the RW Phase. Blood pressure was measured using ABPM. Use of rescue medication was defined as any increase, modification, or addition of antihypertensive medication due to worsening HTN. Treatment discontinuation reports the number of patients who discontinued study treatment in the RW Phase for any reason.
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.populationDescription: The analysis population was patients in the Intent-to-Treat (ITT-RW) Population who met the HTN response criteria at conclusion of the OL Phase. The ITT-RW Population included all patients who were randomized in the RW Phase and received at least 1 dose of study drug post randomization.

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Change in Peak Oxygen Uptake (pVO2) by Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing (CPET)
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: Effect of aficamten compared with metoprolol succinate on exercise capacity in patients with symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). Exercise capacity was determined through changes in peak oxygen uptake (pVO2) after 24 weeks of treatment. pVO2 was measured by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) on a treadmill or bicycle. A higher pVO2 indicates better cardiorespiratory fitness.
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.populationDescription: Full Analysis Set: all randomized participants with available Week 24 pVO2 assessment data

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Change From Baseline in Percent (%) Predicted Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO) Adjusted for Hemoglobin Concentration to Week 24
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: As a measure of pulmonary gas transfer, a standardized lung function test, DLCO, was conducted. The single-breath DLCO test was performed in accordance with American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society (ATS/ERS) guidelines for DLCO testing. Results reported as % predicted DLCO adjusted for hemoglobin concentration (%predicted DLCOadj).

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Complete Response Rate (CRR)
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: CRR is defined as the proportion of patients who achieved a complete response (CR) at the 3-month Visit. A patient was considered a CR if there was no detectable disease in the bladder based on visual observation (white light cystoscopy), biopsy of remaining lesions (if applicable), and voiding urine cytology.
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.populationDescription: All patients who received any dose of UGN-103 (ITT analysis set).

originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.title: Percentage Change From Baseline in Urine Protein to Creatinine Ratio (UPCR)
originalReportedPrimaryOutcomes.description: Percentage reduction in UPCR was obtained from geometric mean ratios. The natural log-transformed ratio of UPCR to its baseline value was analyzed using a Mixed Model for Repeated Measures (MMRM), adjusted by baseline variables specified in the Statistical Analysis Plan (SAP), including data from baseline up to Week 36 during the Double-Blind period.
